page.title: Drive a host from a script
page.description: tinyactors run serves one host over JSON-RPC 2.0 on standard input and output: a script spawns actors, answers their sends and moves the clock.

hero.headline: Drive a host from a script
hero.lede: tinyactors run reads one JSON-RPC request a line and writes what the actors did before each answer. Your script plays the payment service and the clock.

section.heading: Start a host on your charts
section.p: The command compiles the charts into one host, and --io-processor payments names the service your script answers for. The end of standard input ends it.
section.code: tinyactors run --io-processor payments --system shop order.scxml < requests.jsonl
section.p: The order chart asks payments for a charge, retries after 30 seconds of silence, and gives up after three attempts.

section.heading: Answer each send the actor makes
section.p: A run.* method is one of the host's calls, and any other method, such as actor.state, asks the host. Your script answers each effect.send with run.send.

example.caption: The first order is paid and shipped; the second gets no answer, and its charge goes out again at 30 seconds.

section.heading: Answer a send before its sender moves on
section.p: With "hold": true, the turn stops at a send whose sender waits, and answers held. The order stays in paying until request 5 answers and request 6 turns again.
Without it, the sender goes on at once, and a later answer arrives as an ordinary event.

section.heading: Move the clock yourself
section.p: The host's clock moves only with run.advanceTime. Request 14 moves it 30 seconds, and the next turn fires the second order's timeout at once.

claim.statement: A session repeats byte for byte
claim.p: The clock is simulated and Math.random has a fixed seed, so the same requests write the same lines, trace ids included.

section.heading: Generate a client from the schema
section.p: tinyactors run --schema prints the protocol's JSON Schema, every message in both directions. The run command's page serves this release's.

claim.p: It may change in any release until a second client uses it. The schema describes the release you have.
